children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were lower late Wednesday morning, but they were moving away from earlier lows.
An analyst said the canola harvest progress on the Prairies is picking up and that has seen farmers making more deliveries of the oilseed.
Manitoba reported its canola harvest was 43% complete, with below average to average yields.
The analyst also said the market now has a better handle on the size of this year's canola crops. In turn that's essentially eliminated in the risk premium that was in the oilseed.

He added that declines in Chicago soyoil have been pressuring canola prices and its crush margins. Plus news of China buying canola from Australia for the first time since 2020 also weighed on prices in North America.
Declines in the Chicago soy complex were pressuring canola, while European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil were mixed, offering little direction.
Crude oil prices have turned around with gains becoming sharper.
The Canadian dollar continued its downturn on late Wednesday morning, with the loonie at 70.94 U.S. cents, compared with Tuesday's close of 71.10.
